learn: Personal space is the bubble around your body.
When we move, we keep our bubble from popping into someone else's.
Stretch your arms out and turn around. That is your space.
check: How do you find your space?
When we move, we keep our bubble...
lessons.try: Stand still and stretch out your arms to find your personal space.

learn: General space is all the space we share, like the whole gym or playground.
We move through general space without bumping.
Look up and around so you can see where to go.
check: How do we move through general space?
Where should you look when moving?
lessons.try: Walk around a room without touching anyone or anything.

learn: Good movers listen for signals.
A whistle or a "freeze" means stop right away.
Stopping safely keeps everyone safe.
lessons.try: Play a stop-and-go game with a grown-up calling "go" and "freeze".

learn: We can move from place to place in many ways.
Walking, running and jumping are all ways to move.
When you jump, bend your knees to land softly.
check: Which is a way to move?
How do you land a jump softly?
lessons.try: Walk, run, then jump in place three times.

learn: Hopping is jumping on one foot.
Galloping is like a horse: one foot always leads.
Skipping is a step and a hop, then switch feet.
lessons.try: Gallop like a horse across the room.

learn: We can move forward, backward and sideways.
We can also move high, like reaching for the sky, or low, like a crawling turtle.
Moving in all ways makes our bodies strong.
check: Moving in all ways makes our bodies...
lessons.try: Walk forward, backward and sideways.

learn: Balance is staying steady without falling.
When we balance, we hold our body still.
Looking at one spot helps you balance.
check: When we balance, we hold our body...
lessons.try: Stand on one foot and count to five.

learn: You can balance on two feet, one foot, or two hands and two feet.
More body parts touching the ground is easier.
Fewer body parts touching the ground is harder.
check: Which is easier to balance on?
More parts on the ground is...
Can you balance on hands and feet?
lessons.try: Balance on two hands and one foot like a table missing a leg.

learn: Walk on a line on the floor like a tightrope walker.
Hold your arms out to the sides to help.
Go slowly and look ahead.
check: How should you walk on a line?
lessons.try: Walk along a line of tape on the floor without stepping off.

learn: To throw underhand, swing your arm low like a pendulum.
Step forward with the foot opposite your throwing hand.
Let go when your hand points at the target.
check: When your hand points at the target
lessons.try: Throw a soft ball underhand to a grown-up.

learn: Watch the ball all the way into your hands.
Make a basket with your hands and pull the ball in to your body.
Start with a soft, big ball.
check: What do you watch when catching?
How do you hold your hands?
What ball is best to start?
lessons.try: Catch a soft ball five times.

learn: You can roll a ball along the ground to a friend.
You can bounce a ball and catch it.
Push the ball down with your fingers, not a slap.
check: How do you bounce a ball?
Can you roll a ball to a friend?
lessons.try: Bounce and catch a ball five times.

learn: Germs are tiny living things too small to see.
Some germs can make us sick.
Washing hands removes germs.
check: Can you see germs with just your eyes?
How do we remove germs from hands?
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up what germs are.

learn: Wet your hands, add soap and rub for 20 seconds.
Scrub the backs of your hands, between your fingers and under your nails.
Rinse and dry with a clean towel.
check: What do you use with water?
lessons.try: Wash your hands while singing "Happy Birthday" twice.

learn: Wash your hands before you eat.
Wash after using the toilet, after playing outside and after blowing your nose.
Cough or sneeze into your elbow.
check: When should you wash your hands?
Should you wash after using the toilet?
lessons.try: Name three times you should wash your hands.

learn: Teeth help us bite, chew and talk.
Children lose baby teeth and grow adult teeth.
We take care of teeth so they stay strong.
check: What do teeth help us do?
They fall out and adult teeth grow
lessons.try: Count your teeth in the mirror with a grown-up.

learn: Brush your teeth two times a day, in the morning and before bed.
Use a pea-sized dot of toothpaste.
Brush for two minutes, all the sides of every tooth.
lessons.try: Brush your teeth for two minutes tonight.

learn: Sugary foods and drinks can hurt teeth.
Water, milk, fruit and vegetables are good for teeth.
A dentist checks teeth to keep them healthy.
lessons.try: Pick a tooth-friendly snack.

learn: Food gives our bodies energy to play, grow and learn.
Different foods help our bodies in different ways.
Eating many kinds of foods keeps us healthy.
check: Should we eat many kinds of food?
lessons.try: Name three foods you ate today.

learn: Fruits and vegetables are colourful and full of vitamins.
Grains like bread and rice give energy. Proteins like beans, eggs and fish help muscles grow.
Dairy like milk and cheese helps bones get strong.
lessons.try: Make a pretend plate with one food from each group.

learn: Everyday foods are healthy foods we can eat often, like fruits and vegetables.
Sometimes foods are treats, like cake and candy. We eat them only sometimes.
Water is the best drink when you are thirsty.
check: What is the best drink when you are thirsty?
lessons.try: Sort five foods into everyday and sometimes foods.

learn: Our bodies need to move every day.
Playing, running, dancing and riding bikes are all good exercise.
Exercise makes our heart and muscles strong.
lessons.try: Do one minute of jumping jacks.

learn: Your heart pumps blood all around your body.
When you run, your heart beats faster.
When you rest, your heart slows down.
check: When you run, your heart beats...
lessons.try: Feel your heartbeat, run in place, then feel it again.

learn: Sleep helps your body grow and your brain remember.
Young children need lots of sleep, about 10 to 13 hours.
A calm bedtime routine helps you fall asleep.
check: About how much sleep do young children need?
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up your bedtime routine.

learn: Everyone has feelings.
We can feel happy, sad, angry, scared, excited or calm.
All feelings are okay to have.
check: Are all feelings okay to have?
lessons.try: Make a happy face, a sad face and a surprised face.

learn: When we feel angry or upset, we can calm down.
Take slow, deep breaths. Smell the flower, blow out the candle.
Counting to ten or hugging a soft toy can help too.
check: "Smell the flower, blow out the candle" is for...
lessons.try: Take three slow breaths: smell the flower, blow out the candle.

learn: We use words to say how we feel: "I feel sad because..."
Talking to a trusted grown-up can help when you have a big feeling.
We notice how others feel and are kind.
check: Who can help with big feelings?
When a friend is sad, we...
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up about a time you felt happy.

learn: Some things at home are not safe to touch, like a hot stove or medicine.
Only a grown-up gives you medicine.
If you are not sure something is safe, ask a grown-up first.
check: Is a hot stove safe to touch?
If you are not sure, you...
lessons.try: With a grown-up, find three things at home that are not for kids to touch.

learn: Hold a grown-up's hand when crossing the street.
Stop, look left, look right, and look left again before crossing.
Cross at a crosswalk and wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
check: Whose hand do you hold to cross?
What do you wear on a bike?
lessons.try: Practise "stop, look left, look right, look left" with a grown-up.

learn: In an emergency, a grown-up can call 911.
If you are lost, stay where you are and ask a police officer or a parent with children for help.
Your body belongs to you. If anyone makes you feel unsafe, tell a trusted grown-up.
check: What number is called in an emergency?
Stay where you are and ask for help
If someone makes you feel unsafe, you...
lessons.try: Practise what you would say if you got lost.
